commands.author: snotty

target.title: fix(message): ignore populated location on text sends
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a Telegram delivery failure where model-generated `message(action="send")` calls could populate the optional `location` object during an ordinary text or media reply. Shared outbound validation correctly rejects mixed location + content payloads, so an otherwise complete visible reply was dropped.

## Root Cause

Telegram contributes a `location` object to the existing `send` action. Some model/tool-call generators populate optional structured fields even when the intended send is ordinary text or media. Treating this as valid globally would weaken the public mixed-payload contract and could silently discard intentional location data for direct callers.

## Why This Change Was Made

The final design preserves the existing public action vocabulary and fixes only the trusted model-input boundary:

- retains the existing location-only `message(action="send")` contract; no new shared action is added;
- marks agent message-tool calls with a private internal origin;
- removes incidental Telegram `location` only from model-authored sends that also contain real text/media/presentation content;
- uses the same private host-owned normalizer in local `runMessageAction` and Gateway `message.action` paths;
- leaves direct/API mixed payloads untouched so existing downstream validation still rejects them;
- keeps standalone Telegram pins/venues valid and source-reply mirroring complete;
- scopes Telegram's location object schema to the current Telegram channel so it does not replace the generic string `location` used by actions such as Discord `event-create` in unscoped tools;
- recognizes the Telegram `image` alias in both delivery and source-reply transcript mirroring.

## User Impact

Normal Telegram text and media replies—including image aliases, attachments, URL/path, and base64 buffer media—are delivered when a model fills an unrelated location field. Intentional standalone location sends remain native pins/venues. Direct/API callers still receive the documented mixed-payload error instead of having location data silently removed.

## Evidence

### Current-head real Telegram Bot API proof

A temporary, uncommitted runner loaded the real current-head Telegram adapter/runtime and delivered through the Telegram Bot API to a live chat. Credentials and target are redacted; the runner is not part of the PR.

- Exact proof head: `fefb8770edabd65f7b0999dff3c5145c643b3b62`
- Redacted transcript: https://gist.github.com/snotty/d3ca4e6b5d473b8513570bb7dab007ea
- Raw transcript: https://gist.githubusercontent.com/snotty/d3ca4e6b5d473b8513570bb7dab007ea/raw/pr111404-live-telegram-proof.txt
- SHA-256: `e2f884f3232ece16f5e1570ce8859d9146318967a40a5a4f8a0234195ae9338e`

Observed live results:

```text
sendMessage -> messageId 8800: incidental-location text delivered; location removed
sendPhoto   -> messageId 8801: incidental-location image delivered; location removed
sendLocation -> messageId 8802: standalone location delivered; location preserved
direct mixed content+location -> rejected before delivery with the existing error
```

The final post-proof ancestry merge touched only shared node-resolution files and did not modify any PR-owned file. Exact-head source tests and full validation remain green after that merge.

Earlier native Telegram Desktop evidence remains useful as before/after proof of the original visible failure:

- Run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29691948840
- Artifact: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29691948840/artifacts/8444147473

## Validation

Exact-head validation after the private-contract redesign and current-main refresh:

```text
Focused message/Telegram suites: passed
  - normalizer: 12 tests
  - Gateway send/source-reply: 82 tests
  - runner validation: 33 tests
  - message-tool schema: 145 tests
  - Telegram action/runtime contract: 101 tests
Production TypeScript: passed
Test TypeScript: passed
Full build: passed, including Control UI performance budgets
Plugin SDK API baseline: passed
Focused formatting: passed
Focused lint: 0 warnings, 0 errors
git diff --check: passed
```

Regression coverage verifies:

- no shared `send-location` action or Plugin SDK action-union expansion remains;
- current-channel schemas are not merged into unscoped message tools;
- Telegram's object location schema applies only in current Telegram context;
- model-authored text/image/buffer/attachment sends drop incidental location;
- location-only `send` remains intact;
- direct/API mixed sends remain strict;
- local and Gateway normalization paths agree;
- `image` reaches durable Telegram delivery and source-reply transcript mirroring;
- location-only terminal source replies mirror formatted location text and complete restart-recovery bookkeeping.
